title: Is the pin real, and can you win the piece?
outcomes: Judges whether a pin is real by asking whether the pinned piece may still move on the line
Wins a pinned piece by adding attackers, using the cheapest attacker first
Predicts how one extra defender changes the count

steps.text: From **Pins: cannot move, or should not move** you know what a pin is. Now judge whether it is real and how to win the piece. A knight pinned to the king cannot move at all. A pinned rook or bishop may still slide along the pin line, even capture the pinner. The best attacker of a pinned piece is usually a **pawn**: it is the cheapest, and a piece pinned to the king cannot run.

steps.caption: White to move. The knight on d5 is pinned to the king by the rook on d1.

line.say: The pawn attacks the pinned knight. The knight cannot move away.
The king steps off the file, ending the pin, but it is White's move.

claims.statement: The knight has no legal move: it is pinned.
e4 wins the knight along the engine line.

steps.text: To win a pinned piece, multiply attackers and count: attackers against defenders, cheapest capture first. **Rule of thumb:** one extra defender can turn a win into an even trade, so recount whenever the position changes. Also check whether the pinned piece can slide along the line: if it can, it is only half pinned and an attack does not trap it.
